intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: SP+'s problem is the defense: #72 in its split against SEI's #25. The scoreboard agrees with SP+ — 38 points allowed at Boise State, 31 at Tulane — and that Tulane loss at #114 in SP+ is indefensible. But SEI reads the underlying game: defensive third-down passing PPA z +2.01 (97th percentile) and offensive early-down pass PPA +2.77, first in the entire sample. Off #22, def #25 is a solid two-sided team. The week's biggest disagreement, and SEI refuses to discount the metrics for two road losses.
hints: Strongest metrics: Early pass PPA +2.77, 3rd pass PPA +2.01, Pen yd +1.60.

teams.explanation: The entire gap is offense: SP+ has it #10, SEI has it #39. The record (8-1) flatters the profile. Houston 28-26, Arizona 34-26, West Virginia 53-48 — three wins by a single possession, and the +98 point differential never gets near top-15 company. SP+ stays patient because early-down rush PPA (z +1.55) and takeaways (INT% z +2.32) test well. The loss at Cincinnati, 37-24, is the one result that reads the way SEI's numbers say it should.
hints: Strongest metrics: INT% +2.32, Early rush PPA +1.55.

teams.explanation: SEI still carries Nebraska with its defense: #18, with defensive third-down pass PPA at z +2.21. Offense #28 with red-zone finishing (+2.36) keeps the projection top-15. SP+'s #34 offense matches what the scoreboard currently says: four straight losses — Indiana 20-17 (an SP+ top-5 team), 17-14 at Oregon, 17-10 to Washington, 24-13 at Illinois. None were blowouts. The disagreement is interpretive: SEI says the play held up and only the wins stopped; SP+ treats the wins as the evidence.
hints: Strongest metrics: RZ TD% +2.36, 3rd pass PPA +2.21, 3rd pass PPA +1.85.
Weakest metrics: Pen -1.73, Pen yd -1.64, Fum% -1.55.
3 of 7 games decided by <=7 pts (SP+ penalizes close wins harder than SEI does).

teams.explanation: SEI's #2 rests on the most disruptive profile in the sport: opponents' early-down rush PPA z +2.45 (99th percentile), offensive explosiveness +2.31, points per drive +2.17. SP+ sits six spots lower because two results stick out — 26-10 at Tennessee and 20-17 at home to Georgia — while the halves (#7 off, #14 def) are strong, not singular. Ball security (fumble rate z -1.50) is mid-tier. SEI trusts the tape over those two scores, and 31-13 at an SP+ top-10 LSU team just added evidence.
hints: Strongest metrics: Early rush PPA +2.45, Exp +2.31, Pts/drive +2.17.

teams.explanation: The gap is the defense. SEI's offense #2 matches SP+'s #1 — points per drive z +2.58, third-down pass PPA +2.40, both first in the sample — but SEI's defense at #47 drags them back to #9. SP+ accepts def #14 and lets the offense carry the rating: 8-1, +162 margin, 45-6 at Stanford, 41-13 at Clemson. Then Notre Dame — SP+ #2 — scored 31 in a 31-24 loss. That is exactly what a #47 defense looks like against a real one; SP+ hasn't seen one yet.
hints: Defense drives the gap: SEI off #2 vs def #47.
Strongest metrics: Pts/drive +2.58, 3rd pass PPA +2.40, Early pass PPA +2.10.

teams.explanation: SP+'s #1 is built on the margin: a +31.3 rating, 70-20 Western Kentucky, 45-17 at Arkansas, 42-7 at Ole Miss. SEI is less convinced, because Georgia's per-play profile is more good than overwhelming: explosiveness +1.82, third-down pass PPA +1.73, early-down rush +1.71. The 27-24 home loss to Auburn (SP+ #60) drags SEI; SP+ barely flinches. Both boards agree on who Georgia beat. The argument is about who it padded.
hints: Strongest metrics: Exp +1.82, 3rd pass PPA +1.73, Early rush PPA +1.71.

teams.explanation: SP+'s #3 forgives three losses — 24-23 at Texas (#5), 30-18 at USC (#18), 41-28 at home to Oregon (#15) — and its halves (#4 off, #1 def) say schedule-adjusted play is elite. SEI stays closer to the tape: offense #9, defense #16, with the best metric prints (forced fumbles +2.11, early-down pass PPA +1.83) short of SP+'s verdict. The margin (+156) is still enormous, but Oregon just hung 41 on this defense — second week in a row it looked beatable.
hints: Strongest metrics: Fum% +2.11, Early pass PPA +1.83, AR +1.75.
